title: Common affine neighbourhood of finitely many points of local dimension at most one
statement: Let $Z$ be a separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism] such that every quasi-compact open subscheme of $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in Z$, where $r\geq0$, and assume that each local ring $\mathcal O_{Z,z_i}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there is an affine open subscheme $U\subseteq Z$ containing every $z_i$. Affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; for $r=0$ the empty affine open is allowed.

proof.text: If $r=0$, take the empty open, which is $\operatorname{Spec}(0)$. Otherwise let $T=\{z_1,\ldots,z_r\}$. Choose an affine open $W_i$ about each $z_i$ using the local affineness in the definition of a scheme, and set $W=\bigcup_i W_i$. Each $W_i$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. A cover of $W$ restricts to a cover of each of these finitely many quasi-compact subsets; the union of the resulting finite subcovers covers $W$. Thus $W$ is a quasi-compact open containing $T$, and the hypothesis supplies finitely many irreducible components of $W$. Neighbourhoods inside $W$ are cofinal among neighbourhoods in $Z$, so restriction identifies $\mathcal O_{W,z_i}=\mathcal O_{Z,z_i}$. It suffices to find the required affine open in $W$, since an open of an open is open.

Let $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ be the irreducible components of $W$ with their reduced induced closed structures, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each $C_a$ is nonempty, reduced, and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Both $W$ and each $C_a$ are separated: for either inclusion $Y\hookrightarrow Z$ (the open inclusion $W\hookrightarrow Z$ or the composite $C_a\hookrightarrow W\hookrightarrow Z$), the diagonal $Y\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y$ is the pullback of $\Delta_Z$ along $Y\times Y\to Z\times Z$. Indeed an open inclusion is a monomorphism by restriction of the structure sheaf, and a closed inclusion is a monomorphism because its point map is injective and its sheaf map is surjective. Their composite is therefore a monomorphism. For any test scheme $S$, two maps $a,b:S\to Y$ have equal composites in $Z$ exactly when $a=b$; this identifies the pullback of $\Delta_Z$ with $Y$ and its map to $Y\times Y$ with $\Delta_Y$. Since $\Delta_Z$ is closed and closed immersions are preserved by base change, this diagonal is closed.

source.place: Tag 09NN, proof, reduction by Tag 09NM; reduced structures from Tag 01J3 (schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), and base change from Tag 01JY (schemes-lemma-base-change-immersion).

proof.text: Fix $a$ and $z_i\in C_a$, and write $A=\mathcal O_{W,z_i}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{C_a,z_i}$. For the closed immersion $i:C_a\hookrightarrow W$, the surjection $\mathcal O_W\to i_*\mathcal O_{C_a}$ in [def-weil-closed-immersion] means that a section of the target sheaf lifts on a neighbourhood of each point. Represent an element of its stalk by a section, choose such a lift near $z_i$, and take its germ. Every neighbourhood of $z_i$ in $C_a$ is the intersection with an ambient neighbourhood, so the germ description in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] identifies the target stalk with $B$. We obtain a surjective ring map $f:A\to B$. For any ideal $J\subseteq B$, choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $f^{-1}(J)$ in the Noetherian ring $A$. Each $b\in J$ lifts to this inverse image; expressing a lift as $\sum c_j a_j$ gives $b=\sum f(c_j)f(a_j)$. Thus the $f(a_j)$ generate $J$ and $B$ is Noetherian. Preimages of prime ideals are prime. Moreover surjectivity gives $f(f^{-1}(J))=J$, so inverse images preserve strict inclusions. Every strict prime chain in $B$ therefore gives a chain of the same length in $A$, proving $\dim B\leq\dim A\leq1$. This verifies both hypotheses at every selected point of every component, including points on several components.

source.place: Tag 09NN, proof, componentwise reduction: explicit quotient-ring check of the hypotheses of Tag 09NJ.

proof.text: For each $a$, the set $T_a=T\cap C_a$ is finite, $C_a$ is integral and separated by step 2, and its local rings at the points of $T_a$ satisfy the hypotheses by step 3. Apply [lem-trf-integral-codimension-one-affine-neighbourhood] to obtain an affine open $V_a\subseteq C_a$ containing $T_a$. If $T_a$ is empty one may use the empty affine open.

source.place: Tag 09NN, proof, last sentence, invoking Tag 09NJ (lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-componentwise-finite-set-affine-neighbourhood] to $W$, its finitely many reduced irreducible components $C_a$, and the affine opens $V_a$ from step 4. All its hypotheses are now verified; it gives an affine open $U\subseteq W$ containing $T$. Its composite open inclusion into $Z$ makes it the affine open required in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-0df9da17d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Pass with no changes. The item is a split of Stacks 09NN (varieties.tex l.9141-9156) into two new nodes and three reduction steps. The new nodes are lem-trf-integral-codimension-one-affine-neighbourhood, which matches 09NJ (l.9016-9058) exactly: integral, separated, finite T, selected local rings Noetherian of dimension at most 1. The other is lem-trf-componentwise-finite-set-affine-neighbourhood, which matches 09NM (l.9083-9136) exactly: finitely many components, each component's share of T inside an affine open of its reduced structure. The tags agree with tags/tags l.12217/12220/12221. Step 1: the finite union of the affine opens around the points is quasi-compact (lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs), so the hypothesis gives finitely many components, and the local rings are unchanged. Step 2: components get the reduced induced structure (lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (2)) and are integral by def-pc-integral-scheme; they are separated because the inclusions are monomorphisms, so their diagonal is a pullback of Z's closed diagonal and stays closed under base change (lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change). Step 3, elementary: the closed immersion gives a surjection of local rings, and Noetherianity and dimension at most 1 pass to the quotient; this holds at intersection points and with nilpotents. Steps 4 and 5 meet exactly the hypotheses of 09NJ and 09NM. Small cases checked: empty selection, a generic point, the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring, two points on P^1, the line with doubled origin (shows separatedness is needed), crossing lines at the crossing point, and nonreduced schemes. Neither new node restates the item. A whole-DAG search for these tags and for 'affine open containing a finite set' statements found no duplicates; the quasi-projective, Hilbert-scheme and generic-point nodes are not equivalent. There is no SGA citation, no repair note for this item, and no tool_uses. This is the fourth identical delivery (after 8a5454, 4a1916 and 13199d); compared with 13199d only the wording of step 3 changed, and both new nodes are unchanged apart from split_report and mathlib_searches. Maintainer note: repeated live-DAG promotion redeliveries of an unchanged split.
